properties.label: Declared burn duration
properties.description: Initial fuel duration; the consuming action controls how it is converted to active fire time.

properties.label: Chopping capability
properties.description: The tool's chopping parameter; some recipes test it as a nonconsumed tool requirement.

properties.label: Base crafting cost
properties.description: The recipe's declared AP cost before station and skill reductions.

properties.label: Base recipe yield
properties.description: The declared crafting yield; in-place actions such as Finish Raft are not ordinary inventory outputs.

properties.label: Cutting capability
properties.description: The tool's cutting parameter, before action-specific calculations.

properties.label: Damage class identifier
properties.description: Identifier corresponding to the game's damage-type records, not a damage amount.

properties.label: Base maximum durability
properties.description: Declared maximum durability, not the condition of an individual generated or used item.

properties.label: Initializer value
properties.description: Literal database value before recipe postprocessing, durability and trade adjustments; not a guaranteed merchant price.

properties.label: Initializer weight
properties.description: Literal weight before the recipe postprocessing pass and runtime modifiers.

properties.label: Insulation parameter
properties.description: The declared insulation parameter, before equipment and environmental effects.

properties.label: Base item action cost
properties.description: The initializer's general item action-cost field; particular actions and skills may use or modify it differently.

properties.label: Declared armor
properties.description: Armor field on the item definition; placement and combat rules determine its effect.

properties.label: Melee pattern total maximum
properties.description: Sum of encoded positive pattern cells, before target overlap, armor and modifiers; not guaranteed actual damage per attack.

properties.label: Melee pattern total minimum
properties.description: Sum of encoded positive pattern cells, before target overlap, armor and modifiers; not guaranteed actual damage per attack.

properties.label: Declared spark chance
properties.description: An ignition component, not the overall chance to light a fire.

properties.label: Base stack limit
properties.description: Maximum stack count declared by the initializer.

properties.label: Waterproofing parameter
properties.description: The declared waterproofing parameter used by wetness and drying logic.

properties.label: Equip cost
properties.description: Base equipment action cost from the item's inventory footprint, distinct from attacking or using the item.

properties.label: Attack range
properties.description: Literal weapon reach from the item definition, measured in tiles.

properties.label: Base block chance
properties.description: Innate chance to stop a whole attack; Shield Savant adds to an equipped shield's value.

Craft through the player's crafting menu: 2 [[Twine]], 2 [[Branch (Trollgnarl)]] and 10 [[Spider Silk]] produce one bow for a base cost of 8 AP. This recipe is available in the tester, not in stable 0.9.6.5.

The listed weight is the base definition's 0.65 kg. Crafting recalculates weight from the components; the effective weight can therefore differ. Its declared value alone does not establish merchant stock.
Its base attack uses [[Piercing]] damage. The pattern shows potential per-cell damage, not guaranteed damage to a target.
The base item action cost is 6 AP rather than stable 0.9.6.5's 6.4 AP. The tester adds Push, Pull and Board to the context menu; Push and Pull each cost 6 AP.

Push targets a free tile 16 pixels away. AP is spent before the destination check, so a blocked push still costs AP. Pull moves the player 3 pixels away and then moves the raft toward that position; push nudges the player 3 pixels toward it.

Direct boarding requires being within 8 pixels; otherwise interaction opens the context menu. Push/pull motion takes time and its destination is not saved. No persistence of an in-progress movement is promised.

A burning [[Campfire]] now offers the recipe: 1 [[Spider Meat]] produces 1 Grilled Spider Meat for 2.4 base AP. The recipe values are unchanged; the tester adds actual menu access. [[Survivor's Field Kit]] does not receive this recipe.
When burning, the tester's cooking menu includes [[Grilled Spider Meat]]: 1 [[Spider Meat]] yields 1 grilled meat for 2.4 base AP.
The new [[Grilled Spider Meat]] cooking-menu access belongs to a burning [[Campfire]], not this field kit.

Newly generated areas can now get the special spider-cave entrance. Approximately one third of eligible ordinary small-cave candidates become this entrance after cave selection and collision checks; this is not an area-wide encounter probability. Previously saved areas do not receive the entrance when revisited.

The cave layout, webs, treasure, [[Mirk Lurker]] and [[Deathlob]] were already defined in stable 0.9.6.5. Their base stats are unchanged. A displayed cave name is unconfirmed; cave-like and dungeon-like classifications differ.

Outside selection also gives Deathlob a relative weight of 0.125 in [[Sunken Ancient Ruins]] and 0.1 in other general outside areas. These are not 12.5% and 10% encounter probabilities; normal population caps and other gates still apply.
Deathlob is included in the outside enemy pool with a relative selection weight of 0.125. This is not a 12.5% encounter chance and does not bypass the normal spawn conditions.

Outside-area replenishment has a new outer 50% gate before existing checks. All trees are counted, with fewer than 4.25 special resources overall and fewer than one per tree. A tree still needs at least 12 branches and must pass the 1.5% tree roll before branch selection plus the remaining branch checks. This is not 50% per tree or a guaranteed minimum distance between honey-bearing trees.
Branch death chance is quartered within the 16-pixel view margin. Outside it, activated trees with average branch life at most 0.01 have a 1% removal roll per check.

Log placement is conditional: mossy-log tiles within 128 pixels reduce the attempted line length, and the attempt requires a positive existing log count. Terrain, obstruction and ground-cover checks still apply. A dead tree is removed even if no logs are placed, so replacement logs are not guaranteed.
With no sickness effect, the accidental 0.16 wellbeing increase is removed and sickness time is reset. Sickness levels retain their 1%, 2% and 3% penalties.
The container-collision check is applied only when the tile being checked is within 8 pixels of the proposed placement point. This is not a general container scan over the whole footprint.

The newly accessible spider cave is cave-like but is excluded from the separate dungeon-like classification. Its HUD and temperature/drying calculation use the current weather temperature, not the fixed underground 0.35 value. Do not infer underground exposure rules merely from its cave tiles.

The newly accessible spider cave uses the weather/day clock, not the underground HUD, because it is excluded from the dungeon-like classification. Cave-like geometry does not itself establish underground temperature or display behavior.

Revisiting outside areas other than Rift-Thorn Mire can attempt Fern growth over elapsed days. The 240-hour elapsed-time cap permits up to 10 day iterations, each with up to 256 candidate-position searches. This is ground-cover growth, not new log production.

Activated, almost-dead trees outside the view margin can be removed by a 1% check in the tester. Replacement logs are conditional, not guaranteed; see [[Tree health and chopping#0.9.9.7_tester|the tester's tree and log limits]].
